summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, coronary artery disease, and a history of pancreatitis presented with acute epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting after eating. He was found to have hyperkalemia with associated bradycardia and EKG changes, which resolved with medical treatment and hemodialysis. Imaging confirmed acute pancreatitis with fat stranding in the tail of the pancreas and elevated lipase. His pain improved with NPO status, IV fluids, and analgesia. He was transitioned to a clear diet, then advanced to soft foods, and managed his diabetes with adjusted insulin dosing. He remained stable, with improving labs, and was discharged home with instructions to avoid fatty foods, monitor weight, and continue all home medications including a short course of oral hydromorphone for pain.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
